title: Fix the JPA N+1 with @EntityGraph
summary: An N+1 on the post list gets fixed, then paging is added and quietly loads every row into memory.

turns.user: post list endpoint is slow. turned on show-sql and theres like 200 selects going by

assistant.body: Short answer: a classic N+1. findByPublishedTrue fetches the posts once, then author and comments are LAZY, so every post fires extra selects when the summary touches them. For 100 posts that is up to 1 + 200 queries. An @EntityGraph pulls both into the first query.

turns.user: way faster! now PM wants paging. can I just add a Pageable?

assistant.body: Great question! Yes, add a Pageable parameter and return Page<Post>. The @EntityGraph keeps working, so the N+1 stays fixed. On the service side, Page.map turns each post into the DTO.

turns.user: counts look right but the log says firstResult/maxResults specified with collection fetch; applying in memory. is it reading everything??

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. With a collection like comments fetched in the same query, Hibernate cannot put a LIMIT on the SQL, so it reads every published post and slices the page in memory. The counts were right because it read everything. author is a to-one join, which adds no rows, so it can stay. comments comes out of the graph and loads through default_batch_fetch_size, 100 at a time in an IN list. A page of 20 costs three queries, the count included.

turns.user: review says that setting hits the whole project, not ok. just do it for comments

assistant.body: Understood. The line comes out of application.properties, and Hibernate @BatchSize goes directly on Post.comments. It loads the same way, but only this association is affected.
